label: sparse token-combination detector: f two steps back, then j/f/b/u/e, then 2/3/j/c/a/g
explanation: Very sparse (0.05% of steps). It fires mostly during the original phase at t=2..6 (83% of mass) and never at t=0/1. The weaker remainder is at <DEL> and early copy steps (recall_idx 0 and 2). The strongest single cue is an f input two steps back (prev2_tok=f, 20x lift, 54% of mass), plus prev_tok=j (10x) and in_tok of digit 2/3 or j/c. The top examples look like trigrams such as f j 2 and f f j 3, and first tokens x/1/f/v/q also raise the rate. Even so, every simple predicate has very low precision: prev2=f fires on 165k steps and the feature is active on only 1% of them. The best conjunction (f two back, then j/f/b/u/e, then 2/3/j/c/a/g/<DEL>) reaches dev F1 0.16 with mass recall 0.26. Magnitude rises slightly with predicate coverage (higher quartiles are covered more), but no clear modulator was found. The feature seems to respond to a distributed combination of recent token identities that a boolean predicate does not capture.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: in_tok=2 (+4.74), orig2=f (+3.44), prev_tok=j (+3.26), prev2_tok=f (+3.14), in_tok=3 (+2.73), orig1=f (+2.70). Lower it: recall_idx=5 (-4.84), prev2_tok=- (-3.60), in_tok=f (-3.34), prev_tok=r (-3.21).
